does_not_prove: This register proves that each declared boundary has one owner and a complete clean, refusal, binding, identity, resource, and version-applicability matrix. It does not prove that every workspace boundary was discovered or that one named test completely establishes its axis.

boundaries.authority_owner: The caller owns the admitted compile command and source selection.
boundaries.mechanism_owner: lib_c_facts owns Clang invocation, fact extraction, and bounded diagnostics.
boundaries.effects: Reads source and compile-database files and may invoke the configured Clang frontend.
boundaries.resource_budget: The caller supplies the project scope; diagnostics and subprocess completion are bounded by the library contract.
composition: Policy tools consume typed facts and may not privately reinterpret Clang output.
Analysis failure is returned through p101_error before policy evaluation.

stale_version.reason: The native analysis API is linked C ABI rather than a versioned record boundary.

boundaries.authority_owner: The event schema owns admission; producers do not define consumer policy.
boundaries.mechanism_owner: lib_tool_event owns record encoding, bounded parsing, and schema validation.
boundaries.effects: Parsing is memory-local; writing appends one complete record to the caller-owned stream.
boundaries.resource_budget: One record is bounded by the protocol line and field limits.
composition: Consumers accept typed records and keep analysis policy outside the parser.
collaborators: lib_env emits records without owning analysis policy
tools consume records without private parsers

boundaries.output: next lifecycle state and policy-free lifecycle facts
boundaries.authority_owner: The validated event stream owns lifecycle facts; reporting tools own findings policy.
boundaries.mechanism_owner: lib_tool_event owns policy-free lifecycle state transitions.
boundaries.effects: Allocates bounded replay state and records lifecycle entries in caller-owned storage.
boundaries.resource_budget: Capacity growth is checked for overflow and limited by admitted input size.
composition: Only version-validated records enter the lifecycle reducer.
Reports consume lifecycle facts without duplicating resource semantics.
collaborators: scripts/runtime/p101-view.py owns presentation and teaching advice

stale_version.reason: Lifecycle replay admits already-version-validated event records.

boundaries.output: typed receipt validation status and admitted outcome summary
boundaries.refusal: p101_tool_receipt_validation_status or p101_error for I/O failure
boundaries.evidence: semantic receipt digest plus optional admitted-artifact fingerprint
boundaries.authority_owner: The receipt schema owns admission; the producing tool owns its declared outcome.
boundaries.mechanism_owner: lib_tool_event owns bounded receipt serialization, hashing, and validation.
boundaries.effects: Reads or writes one caller-selected receipt file and fingerprints only admitted artifacts.
boundaries.resource_budget: Receipt bytes, record counts, and artifact admission are explicitly bounded.
composition: The check graph verifies declared receipts before accepting a producer node.
Consumers may trust only fields covered by the validated receipt digest.
collaborators: durable tools own their policy and outcome
the governed check graph requires declared producer receipts

boundaries.input: argv vector and bounded execution options
boundaries.output: child exit status and redirected artifacts
boundaries.authority_owner: The caller owns argv, environment policy, and the meaning of the child result.
boundaries.mechanism_owner: lib_util owns fork/exec, descriptor plumbing, bounded capture, and wait semantics.
boundaries.effects: Creates a child process and caller-declared output files without invoking a shell.
boundaries.resource_budget: Capture limits and process completion policy are supplied in bounded execution options.
composition: Callers construct argv arrays rather than shell command strings.
Child status and capture failures remain distinct typed outcomes.
collaborators: tools construct argv but do not construct shell command strings

stale_version.reason: The subprocess boundary accepts argv and options rather than a versioned protocol.

boundaries.input: wrapper call and resource lifecycle event
boundaries.authority_owner: The wrapper operation owns event meaning; the environment owns observer delivery order.
boundaries.mechanism_owner: lib_env owns sequence allocation, observer dispatch, completion, and sticky write failure.
boundaries.effects: Emits ordered records to caller-selected streams and updates synchronized observer state.
boundaries.resource_budget: Record fields are bounded by the event protocol and stream failures become sticky.
composition: Wrapper libraries describe operations through lib_env hooks.
lib_tool_event owns representation and replay while tools own findings policy.
collaborators: lib_tool_event owns record representation and replay

boundaries.input: validated machine state and one callback decision
boundaries.output: typed step result and emitted effects
boundaries.authority_owner: The bound transition table owns allowed transitions; the application owns effect execution.
boundaries.mechanism_owner: lib_fsm owns one-step validation, transition commitment, refusal, and sequencing.
boundaries.effects: Produces typed effects through the caller-selected sink but does not execute application policy.
boundaries.resource_budget: Machine and effect capacities are checked; one step executes at most one callback decision.
composition: p101_fsm_run is a convenience loop over p101_fsm_step.
Applications interpret effects only after a completed typed transition.
collaborators: p101_fsm_run is only a convenience loop

stale_version.reason: The FSM step API is linked C ABI and has no serialized version boundary.
